note: Hand-maintained, unlike data/index.json. The reader marks the first occurrence of each term in each section and shows this on click. Keys match case-sensitively on whole words, so only add genuinely opaque abbreviations: US, EU, UN and the like are noise, not help. Where an abbreviation has a common other meaning, say so in the gloss — that is the case this file earns its keep on.

AOSIS.gloss: The negotiating bloc of low-lying and island states. Its leverage rests almost entirely on 1.5°C being a commitment rather than a target, which is why it fights framing changes to that number.

BRIC.gloss: A FEMA pre-disaster mitigation grant programme. Nothing to do with the BRICS grouping of states.

CCS.gloss: A US institute, now part of the Council on Strategic Risks. In most other writing CCS means carbon capture and storage; in this digest it does not.

CNA.gloss: A US non-profit research organisation, formerly the Center for Naval Analyses. Its 2007 Military Advisory Board report put "threat multiplier" into circulation.

COP.gloss: The decision-making body of a UN convention. Which convention depends on context: usually the climate convention, but the desertification and biodiversity conventions have their own numbered COPs.

COP31.expansion: 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN climate convention

CPS.gloss: The UN system's own term for the field, and the job title of the advisers it deploys.

CRS.gloss: The US Congress's in-house research arm.

CSDP.gloss: The EU's framework for military and civilian crisis-management missions.

CSM.gloss: The joint UN unit run by DPPA, UNDP, UNEP and DPO. The field's only standing multilateral machinery.

CSR.gloss: The US institute that houses the Center for Climate and Security.

CWP.gloss: The European Commission's annual list of what it intends to propose, and when.

D66.gloss: Dutch social-liberal party; leads the cabinet sworn in February 2026.

DG CLIMA.gloss: The European Commission department that owns the climate file.

DPPA.expansion: UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs

EEAS.gloss: The EU's diplomatic service, and where its climate-security file sits.

ENSO.gloss: The Pacific climate oscillation behind El Niño and La Niña. Its dry teleconnections, not its wet ones, carry most of the measured conflict risk.

FEMA.gloss: The US disaster response and mitigation agency.

GHACOF.expansion: Greater Horn of Africa Climate Outlook Forum
GHACOF.gloss: The regional seasonal-forecast forum, numbered by session.

GLOF.gloss: A flood caused by a glacier-dammed lake draining suddenly. Monitoring in the Himalaya is built around this hazard, which is why an ice-and-rock avalanche can arrive unwatched.

HCSS.expansion: The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies

ICIMOD.expansion: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development
ICIMOD.gloss: The intergovernmental body for the Hindu Kush Himalaya, based in Kathmandu.

IMCCS.expansion: International Military Council on Climate and Security

IOD.gloss: A sea-surface temperature oscillation across the Indian Ocean; both its phases raise conflict risk in strongly connected regions.

IWT.gloss: The 1960 India–Pakistan water-sharing treaty brokered by the World Bank.

KNMI.gloss: The Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute, and one of the partners behind World Weather Attribution.

MEA.gloss: India's foreign ministry. In environmental writing MEA usually means multilateral environmental agreement; here it does not.

MFF.gloss: The EU's seven-year budget. The 2028–2034 round proposes 35 per cent climate and environment mainstreaming, which is not the same as a climate-security line.

MPTF.gloss: The UN pooled-funding vehicle through which member states finance joint programmes.

NDC.gloss: A country's self-set emissions pledge under the Paris Agreement.

NDRRMA.expansion: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority
NDRRMA.gloss: Nepal's disaster agency, and the source of its official casualty figures.

NDS.gloss: The US Department of Defense's periodic strategy document.

NIC.gloss: The US intelligence community's long-range analytic body; publisher of Global Trends.

NOFO.gloss: The instrument that actually releases US federal grant money, so its issue date is when a programme becomes real.

NSIDC.expansion: National Snow and Ice Data Center

NSR.gloss: The Arctic shipping route along Russia's northern coast.

OND.gloss: The short rains season in the eastern Horn of Africa, forecast as a unit.

PCA.gloss: The inter-state arbitration institution seated in The Hague.

PDD.gloss: NATO's communications arm, and the office to ask when a NATO publication quietly stops appearing.

PGA80.expansion: President of the 80th session of the UN General Assembly

PIF.gloss: The regional body of Pacific states; author of the Boe Declaration and the Ocean of Peace Declaration.

PNAS.expansion: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

PSC.gloss: The African Union's standing decision-making organ for conflict prevention and response.

PSI.gloss: The Dutch-founded climate-security platform hosted at Clingendael.

SAS-182.expansion: Systems Analysis and Studies research task group 182
SAS-182.gloss: The NATO Science and Technology Organization group behind The Effects of Climate Change on Security, January 2026.

SCR.gloss: The independent organisation that tracks UN Security Council business. Not a Security Council resolution.

SRM.gloss: Deliberate cooling by reflecting sunlight. Its governance is where the security frame appears to be travelling next.

UNEP.gloss: The UN's environmental authority, based in Nairobi.

UNGA81.expansion: 81st session of the UN General Assembly
UNGA81.gloss: Opened 8 September 2026; high-level week from 22 September.

UNISFA.expansion: UN Interim Security Force for Abyei

WWA.gloss: The research network that publishes rapid studies on whether climate change made a given extreme event more likely.
